transcript.text: Thank you both for these critical updates. Let me address each issue in turn. Martin, the conflict you've identified with Westbridge is disqualifying -- we cannot use a firm whose lead investigator has a prior personal representation relationship with the procurement VP. We'll need to pivot to the approved alternate, Barton & Vale. And I take your point about my own potential conflict: since I approved the procurement VP's compensation last year, I should not be the one approving this charter or serving as the reporting line. The investigation should report directly to the audit committee, and I'll step back from charter approval accordingly. Nadia, the supplemental intake note changes things significantly. The addition of gifts to public officials through the supplier potentially implicates anti-bribery and corruption laws, which broadens the investigation scope. The complainant's request to communicate through outside counsel and restrict identity to the investigation team only are reasonable and should be incorporated into the charter. That supplemental note needs to be circulated immediately to the investigation team and factored into the charter. I also want to confirm that preservation has been ongoing from the original hotline allegation intake and now needs to be expanded to cover the supplemental allegations as well. Given all of this, I'd like to propose the following: Barton & Vale as the investigator, reporting directly to the audit committee, an investigation scope that covers both the original improper benefits allegation and the supplemental public official gifts allegation, preservation retroactive to the original hotline intake, complainant contact through their outside counsel, and identity restricted to the investigation team only. Does anyone see any issues with this approach before we move to finalize?

Third, on the reporting line -- since you're stepping back from charter approval, I recommend we route the proposed charter directly to the audit committee chair for review and approval, with me as the point of contact for the investigation team. Fourth, on the expanded scope -- the public official gifts allegation may require separate consideration of voluntary self-disclosure obligations, and I'd like to flag that for the audit committee as part of the charter package. Finally, on preservation -- I'll confirm that the litigation hold is expanded to cover the supplemental allegations and that Barton & Vale's collection plan accounts for both the original and updated intake materials.
